reader.requirement: At --std 85, UNSTRING raises the overflow condition (a) at initiation when the POINTER item's value is below 1 or above the CURRENT size of identifier-1, including a variable-length identifier-1 whose current size is zero (1985 has no zero-length termination rule), and (b) when every receiving area has been acted upon and identifier-1 still has unexamined characters; otherwise no overflow.
reader.edition-search: grep of DialectLevel|CobolVersion|DialectBehaviors|ConstructDialectStatus|EditionContext|Edition.Year over StringEmitter.cs, CobolStringOps.cs, StringUnstringBinder.cs (ctx.Edition there is only the diagnostic sink), EcEmitter#EmitOverflow (>>TURN-gated only); grep of ZeroLength in WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions and DialectBehavior.cs: no behaviour for the zero-length sender. The 2023 GR2 guard `if (src.Length != 0)` in EmitUnstring runs at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 2023 (§2023:14.9.48.4 GR2) a zero-length identifier-1 terminates the statement before the overflow test; 1985 has no such rule, so its GR17a overflow applies (POINTER value 1 > size 0). The compiler takes the 2023 arm at 85.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f14_05 covers the pointer-out-of-range and unexamined-characters overflows on fixed-length senders; not exercised: a variable-length (ODO) sender, including one of current size zero, a trailing delimiter or ALL run that exhausts the sender, and the separate-sign examination size.

reader.notes: Every fixed-length and nonzero variable-length overflow case conforms. The divergence is the zero-length sender: PB1184 added the 2023 GR2 guard `if (src.Length != 0)` around the whole statement with no edition test, so at 85 an ODO sender of current size 0 with POINTER 1 skips the GR17a overflow and ON OVERFLOW never runs. Whether a zero-size ODO group is an ordinary 1985 sender is the one judgement made here (§1985 OCCURS SR5 allows integer-1 = 0); the GR17a text itself is unambiguous.
reader.at-2023: prints X=[QQQ] P=01 with neither phrase run, which is correct at 2023 by §2023:14.9.48.4 GR2

UNSTRING WS-OG INTO WS-X WITH POINTER WS-P ON OVERFLOW DISPLAY "OVERFLOW" NOT ON OVERFLOW DISPLAY "NO OVERFLOW". (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/work-1985-114/unszero.cob, --std 85)
reader.expected: "An UNSTRING is initiated, and the value in the data item referenced by identifier-7 is less than 1 or greater than the size of the data item referenced by identifier-1" causes an overflow condition (§1985:VI.6.27.4 GR17a), and then control goes to imperative-statement-1 (GR18): OVERFLOW is displayed.
reader.observed: Neither OVERFLOW nor NO OVERFLOW is displayed; X=[QQQ] P=01. EmitUnstring wraps the statement in the zero-length guard at every edition.
reader.known_note: none for 1985; PB1184 (landed) introduced the unconditional 2023 GR2 guard and names only --std 2023/2014
